instruction: UX-прогон Bossman (tools/ux_soak) зафиксировал 42 находки high: когда задач больше 500, команда `bossman list tasks --json --limit 1000` возвращает ровно 500 задач, хотя API держит 837 (cli=500 api=837). Найди причину в command-center/bcc/terminal_cli/cli.py (list_items, ветка tasks; маршрут GET /api/tasks в command-center/bcc/api.py читай, но не меняй) и исправь так, чтобы явный --limit N возвращал min(N, всего) задач, новые первыми, без повторов; малые лимиты и пустое хранилище работают как раньше. Сначала напиши тест, который падает на старом коде, в НОВОМ файле command-center/tests/test_terminal_task_paging.py со своим маленьким поддельным клиентом (у поддельного клиента метод get(path, params=None)). ОБЪЁМ (жёстко): меняй только command-center/bcc/terminal_cli/cli.py и создай только этот один новый тест-файл; существующие тесты и файлы не редактируй.

+import os
+import sys
+from unittest.mock import Mock
+
+# Ensure the command-center directory is in the path so we can import bcc
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(__file__)))
+
+from bcc.terminal_cli.cli import list_items
+
+def test_list_tasks_paginates_when_limit_exceeds_api_max():
+    # API returns at most 500 per request
+    # We want to test that when limit > 500, we paginate until we get the requested number (or until no more)
+    client = Mock()
+    # Simulate API that has 837 tasks total
+    # First page: 500 tasks (ids 1..500)
+    # Second page: 337 tasks (ids 501..837)
+    # We'll make the client.get return appropriate pages based on params
+    def get_side_effect(path, params=None):
+        if path == "/api/tasks":
+            limit = params.get("limit", 20) if params else 20
+            before_id = params.get("before_id")
+            # We'll simulate that the API returns tasks in descending order by id
+            # and that the total set of task ids is 1..837 (with 837 being the newest)
+            # So without before_id, we get the newest 500: ids 837 down to 338
+            # With before_id, we get the next page of 500 (or less) that are older than before_id
+            if before_id is None:
+                # first page: newest 500
+                start = 837 - 500 + 1  # 338
+                end = 837
+                ids = list(range(end, start-1, -1))  # descending
+            else:
+                # we want tasks with id < before_id, up to limit
+                # before_id is the oldest id from the previous page (the last one we got)
+                # So we want the next batch of ids that are less than before_id
+                # Example: first page gave us ids 837..338, so before_id=338
+                # Then we want ids 337 down to max(1, 338 - limit)
+                end = before_id - 1
+                start = max(1, end - limit + 1)
+                ids = list(range(end, start-1, -1))
+            # Build task dicts
+            rows = [{"id": id_, "status": "pending", "title": f"Task {id_}"} for id_ in ids]
+            return rows
+        return []
+    client.get.side_effect = get_side_effect
+
+    # Call list_tasks with limit=1000
+    result = list_items(client, "tasks", limit=1000)
+
+    # We should get 837 tasks (all available)
+    assert len(result) == 837
+    # Check that the ids are in descending order and contiguous from 837 down to 1
+    expected_ids = list(range(837, 0, -1))
+    actual_ids = [task["id"] for task in result]
+    assert actual_ids == expected_ids
+
+    # Also verify that the client.get was called multiple times (at least 2)
+    assert client.get.call_count >= 2
+
+def test_list_tasks_respects_limit_less_than_api_max():
+    client = Mock()
+    # API returns up to 500, but we only want 50
+    def get_side_effect(path, params=None):
+        if path == "/api/tasks":
+            limit = params.get("limit", 20) if params else 20
+            before_id = params.get("before_id")
+            if before_id is None:
+                start = 837 - limit + 1
+                end = 837
+                ids = list(range(end, start-1, -1))
+            else:
+                end = before_id - 1
+                start = max(1, end - limit + 1)
+                ids = list(range(end, start-1, -1))
+            rows = [{"id": id_, "status": "pending", "title": f"Task {id_}"} for id_ in ids]
+            return rows
+        return []
+    client.get.side_effect = get_side_effect
+
+    result = list_items(client, "tasks", limit=50)
+    assert len(result) == 50
+    # Should be the 50 newest tasks: ids 837 down to 788
+    expected_ids = list(range(837, 837-50, -1))
+    actual_ids = [task["id"] for task in result]
+    assert actual_ids == expected_ids
+    # Only one call needed because 50 <= 500
+    assert client.get.call_count == 1
+
+def test_list_tasks_works_with_other_types_unchanged():
+    # Ensure we didn't break list_items for other types
+    client = Mock()
+    client.get.return_value = [{"id": 1, "name": "Model A"}]
+    result = list_items(client, "models", limit=5)
+    # For models, the function does not use limit parameter (it ignores it and loads from catalog)
+    # So we expect the mock to not be called? Actually the models branch does not call client.get for the list,
+    # except for the discover endpoint. But we are not testing that here.
+    # We just want to make sure we didn't break the existing behavior.
+    # Since we are mocking, we can just check that we get a list.
+    assert isinstance(result, list)
